newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: 80 die in Tajik typhoid epidemic, official says.
newsitem.headline: 80 die in Tajik typhoid epidemic, official says.

text.p: A senior Tajik health official said on Wednesday the former Soviet republic has been unable to stop the spread of a typhoid epidemic which had claimed the lives of at least 80 people.
"We have not been able to stop the typhoid epidemic which is growing all the time," a high-ranking health official in the Tajik capital Dushanbe told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
He said more than 80 people have died in Dushanbe hospitals alone and said there had been about 10,000 cases of typhoid since the beginning of year.
"The total number of dead is probably much higher as many cases have not been registered in rural areas," he said.
Bob McKerrow, head of the International Federation of the Red Cross's regional office in Central Asia, based in Kazakhstan, said: "The figures sound right to me."
The epidemic started with contaminated drinking water which in Dushanbe has not been chlorinated for four months.
McKerrow said warmer weather in the remote, mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan threatens to increase infection.
"The epidemic seems to have reached its peak and appears to be levelling," said McKerrow, who added there were about 100 new cases a day. "But it's likely to rise again in May and June," he said.
Tajikistan, emerging tentatively from a bitter four-year civil war, closed schools in Dushanbe last month in an effort to halt the spread of the disease.
